 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise Andoni Iraola asked for calm after Liverpool lost to Arsenal and Fenerbahce. He said the team must keep perspective and react quickly.
 The defeats left Liverpool nine points behind the Premier League leaders and ended their perfect Champions League start. Iraola said they were “not as bad” as they look now.
 Liverpool visit Crystal Palace on Nov 8. Ryan Gravenberch may return if he can handle heel pain, and Iraola said he is the only injury doubt.
 AI generated
 LIVERPOOL – Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has called for a sense of perspective after consecutive defeats against Arsenal and Fenerbahce dampened the positive mood at Anfield.
 Last week’s 1-0 defeat by the Gunners left the Reds nine points behind the English Premier League leaders. Three days later, Liverpool suffered their first Champions League defeat of the season in Turkey.
 Iraola, in his first campaign as Liverpool boss, admitted that the two losses had hurt as he prepares his team for the trip to struggling Crystal Palace on Nov 8.
 “One week ago in this press conference, we were on a run, everything was in a good place, and we were in a better mood,” the Spaniard told reporters on Nov 6.
 “And now, two defeats, it changes, and it has to change. It has to be like this, in clubs like ours. And now we have to react. After two defeats, we need the win against Palace away.”
 Iraola said that highs and lows were inevitable so early in his reign after he succeeded Arne Slot in June.
 “When we lose a game, everyone is angry, but we have to have some perspective and we know in the process there will be ups and downs,” said the former Bournemouth boss.
 “We are not as bad as we look today, we were not as good as we looked one week ago and we have to have some perspective.
 “This is part of my challenge also in terms of mood for the group.”
 Iraola could welcome back midfielder Ryan Gravenberch against Palace. The Dutchman was an unused substitute in the loss to Arsenal and missed the Fenerbahce game due to heel discomfort.
 “The only doubt we will have is Ryan,” said Iraola. “It’s a matter of pain. Let’s see if he can deal with the pain and help us.” AFP
